report.answer_text:
The WHO Pandemic Agreement, adopted by the World Health Assembly on May 20, 2025, sets out what countries that become parties will do to prevent pandemics, prepare for them, and respond together. A central goal is to make vaccines, tests, and treatments available according to public-health need, not just countries’ ability to pay. (apps.who.int)
Its main commitments are to:
Strengthen prevention and preparedness. Improve disease surveillance and early warning, maintain national preparedness plans, and build resilient health systems and a trained health workforce. The agreement calls for a *One Health* approach, which recognizes the links between human, animal, and environmental health. (apps.who.int)
Make pandemic supplies more accessible. Cooperate on research and development, expand manufacturing across regions, promote technology transfer, and coordinate procurement and distribution through a global supply-chain network. (apps.who.int)
Share information and the benefits it helps produce. The agreement provides for a Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing system that pairs rapid sharing of pathogen samples and genetic sequence data with equitable access to resulting vaccines, tests, and treatments. During a pandemic emergency, participating manufacturers would aim to make 20% of their real-time production of relevant products available to WHO for allocation based on public-health need. That target applies to participating manufacturers, not to each country’s stockpile. (apps.who.int)
Cooperate on financing and implementation. Support preparedness and response at home and internationally, including through a financing mechanism intended to help countries with fewer resources build capacity. (apps.who.int)
Adoption did not make the agreement binding. As of November 24, 2026, the benefit-sharing annex was still under negotiation, with countries aiming to bring it to the World Health Assembly in May 2027. The agreement opens for signature after the annex is adopted and enters into force 30 days after the 60th ratification. It does not give WHO authority to impose lockdowns, vaccine mandates, or travel restrictions. (who.int)

claims.sentence: The WHO Pandemic Agreement, adopted by the World Health Assembly on May 20, 2025, sets out what countries that become parties will do to prevent pandemics, prepare for them, and respond together.
claims.claim: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted by the World Health Assembly on May 20, 2025.
claims.label: supported

pages.label: supported

quotes.text: 1. ADOPTS, pursuant to Article 19 of the Constitution of the World Health Organization, the WHO Pandemic Agreement as annexed to this resolution;

pages.quote_reason: The first quote shows the World Health Assembly adopting the WHO Pandemic Agreement by resolution, and the second quote places a plenary meeting of the Assembly on 20 May 2025, so the claim's facts are backed.
pages.page_reason: The page is WHA78.1 dated 20 May 2025 that states the Health Assembly 'ADOPTS, pursuant to Article 19 of the Constitution... the WHO Pandemic Agreement' and the annex footer records the third plenary meeting on 20 May 2025, which supports the claim.

claims.sentence: The WHO Pandemic Agreement, adopted by the World Health Assembly on May 20, 2025, sets out what countries that become parties will do to prevent pandemics, prepare for them, and respond together.
claims.claim: The WHO Pandemic Agreement sets out what countries that become parties will do to prevent pandemics, prepare for them, and respond together.
claims.label: supported

pages.label: supported

quotes.text: The Parties shall take steps through international collaboration, in bilateral, regional and multilateral settings, to progressively strengthen pandemic prevention and surveillance measures and capacities

Each Party shall develop, in accordance with national and/or domestic context, comprehensive, multisectoral, and, as appropriate, regional, and national pandemic prevention, preparedness and response plan(s)

The Parties shall cooperate, directly or through relevant international organizations, subject to national and/or domestic law and available resources, to sustainably strengthen the pandemic prevention, preparedness and response capacities of all Parties

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state that Parties shall take steps to prevent pandemics, develop prevention, preparedness and response plans, and cooperate to strengthen prevention, preparedness and response capacities, which together cover what the claim says the agreement sets out.
pages.page_reason: The page excerpts from the WHO Pandemic Agreement describe Parties' obligations on pandemic prevention and surveillance, One Health approaches, comprehensive pandemic prevention, preparedness and response plans, and international cooperation to strengthen preparedness and response capacities, which together support the claim that it sets out what Parties will do to prevent, prepare for, and respond to pandemics together.

claims.sentence: A central goal is to make vaccines, tests, and treatments available according to public-health need, not just countries’ ability to pay. (apps.who.int)

quotes.text: Article 13 Supply chain and logistics 1. The “Global Supply Chain and Logistics Network” (hereinafter the “GSCL Network”) is hereby established to enhance, facilitate, and work to remove barriers and ensure equitable, timely, rapid, safe, and affordable access to pandemic-related health products for countries in need
the distribution of these vaccines, therapeutics, and diagnostics shall be on the basis of public health risk and need, with particular attention to the needs of developing countries

pages.quote_reason: The quotes back the core point that distribution of vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics is based on public health risk and need, but they do not state that this is a central goal or explicitly contrast it with ability to pay.
pages.page_reason: The page describes equitable access, distribution based on public health risk and need, and the GSCL Network's equitable allocation of pandemic-related health products, which supports the goal of allocating by need rather than ability to pay, though it does not explicitly state this as a 'central goal' of the agreement.

pages.page_reason: The page's Article 5 states that the Parties shall promote a One Health approach for pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, and the definitions in Article 1 describe the One Health approach, so the claim that the agreement calls for it is supported.

quotes.text: (b) “One Health approach” for pandemic prevention, preparedness and response recognizes that the health of humans is closely linked and interdependent with the health of domestic and wild animals, as well as plants and the wider environment (including ecosystems)

pages.quote_reason: The quote states that the One Health approach recognizes human health is closely linked and interdependent with the health of animals, plants and the wider environment, which covers everything the claim says.
pages.page_reason: The page's definition of the 'One Health approach' states that human health is closely linked and interdependent with the health of domestic and wild animals, plants and the wider environment, and Article 5 says human health is interconnected with animal health and the environment, so the claim is directly supported.

quotes.text: Article 10 Sustainable and geographically diversified local production 1. ensure equitable, timely, rapid, safe, and affordable access to pandemic-related health products for countries in need during public health emergencies of international concern

pages.page_reason: The page excerpts describe provisions on equitable and timely access to pandemic-related health products (e.g., Article 10 on sustainable production to increase access, Article 13 on GSCL Network to ensure equitable access, purchasing provisions promoting access for developing countries), which supports the claim that a main commitment is making pandemic supplies more accessible, though the excerpts do not explicitly label this as the agreement's main commitment.
